From 8558aef4e8a1a83049ab906d21d391093cfa7e7f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Zilin Guan <zilin@seu.edu.cn>
Date: Wed, 28 Jan 2026 15:44:39 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] net: liquidio: Fix off-by-one error in PF setup_nic_devices()
 cleanup

In setup_nic_devices(), the initialization loop jumps to the label
setup_nic_dev_free on failure. The current cleanup loop while(i--)
skip the failing index i, causing a memory leak.

Fix this by changing the loop to iterate from the current index i
down to 0.

Also, decrement i in the devlink_alloc failure path to point to the
last successfully allocated index.

Compile tested only. Issue found using code review.

Fixes: f21fb3ed364b ("Add support of Cavium Liquidio ethernet adapters")
Suggested-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Zilin Guan <zilin@seu.edu.cn>
Reviewed-by: Kory Maincent <kory.maincent@bootlin.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260128154440.278369-3-zilin@seu.edu.cn
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/cavium/liquidio/lio_main.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/cavium/liquidio/lio_main.c
index 1f10b1b22a1e..c1a3df225254 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/cavium/liquidio/lio_main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/cavium/liquidio/lio_main.c
@@ -3750,6 +3750,7 @@ static int setup_nic_devices(struct octeon_device *octeon_dev)
 	if (!devlink) {
 		device_unlock(&octeon_dev->pci_dev->dev);
 		dev_err(&octeon_dev->pci_dev->dev, "devlink alloc failed\n");
+		i--;
 		goto setup_nic_dev_free;
 	}
 
@@ -3765,11 +3766,11 @@ static int setup_nic_devices(struct octeon_device *octeon_dev)
 
 setup_nic_dev_free:
 
-	while (i--) {
+	do {
 		dev_err(&octeon_dev->pci_dev->dev,
 			"NIC ifidx:%d Setup failed\n", i);
 		liquidio_destroy_nic_device(octeon_dev, i);
-	}
+	} while (i--);
 
 setup_nic_dev_done:
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `drivers/net/ethernet/cavium/liquidio/lio_main.c`

1. **Decrement `i` in the `devlink_alloc` failure path** (line after the `dev_err` call):
   - Added `i--;` before the `goto setup_nic_dev_free;` statement.
   - This ensures that when a failure occurs during `devlink_alloc`, the index `i` correctly points to the last successfully allocated device, so the cleanup loop will free only those allocated devices.

2. **Replaced the cleanup loop** (lines starting at `setup_nic_dev_free:`):
   - Changed from `while (i--) { ... }` to `do { ... } while (i--);`.
   - The original loop decremented `i` before executing the loop body, causing the failing index `i` to be skipped and resulting in a memory leak.
   - The new loop executes the body first (for the current `i`) and then decrements, ensuring that the device at the failing index is also freed.

### Relationship between modifications

The two changes work together to correct an off-by-one error in the resource cleanup sequence:

- Without the `i--` in the `devlink_alloc` failure path, `i` would point to the index that **failed** (i.e., for which no device was allocated). The old `while (i--)` loop would skip that index because the decrement happened before the body, causing the device at the previous index (`i-1`) to be leaked.
- Adding `i--` adjusts the index to the last successfully allocated device, and switching to a `do-while` loop ensures that the device at that index (and all previously allocated ones) are freed properly, eliminating the memory leak.
